entries.definition: take without referencing from someone else's writing or speech; of intellectual property
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Theft of words and ideas - a career-ending accusation in academic and literary settings.

entries.definition: with scepticism; in a sceptical manner
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The adverb of *sceptical*: the British spelling, identical in force.

entries.definition: characterized by wisdom, especially the wisdom of God
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Theological, and about wisdom as a body of teaching rather than a trait.

entries.definition: having a difficult and contrary disposition
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Difficult by habit rather than by temper; the contrariness is settled, almost fond.
examples: a cantankerous and venomous-tongued old lady

entries.definition: marked by refinement in taste and manners
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Faintly pitying since the nineteenth century - shabby-genteel is never far away.

entries.definition: express complaints, discontent, displeasure, or unhappiness
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Implies the objection is loud and probably futile.
examples: She has a lot to kick about

entries.definition: show off
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Loud claims covering weakness; it implies the speaker will not back them up.

entries.definition: ill-mannered and coarse and contemptible in behavior or appearance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Clumsiness and stupidity together, with no suggestion it could be helped.

entries.definition: stunningly beautiful
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Overwhelming beauty - lush and a little theatrical.

entries.definition: poor enough to need help from others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Total and grave - without even the means to live.

entries.definition: ruthless in competition
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The bowels were once the seat of pity; without that, the word is opaque.

entries.definition: in a shoddy manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *shoddy*: poor work passed off as sound - the pretence is as much of the charge as the quality.

entries.definition: characteristic of false pride; having an exaggerated sense of self-importance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Excessive pride in appearance or achievement - shallow rather than dangerous.

entries.definition: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Shorter and even softer than 'pass away'; common in American speech.

entries.definition: having a hard nonresonant metallic sound
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Harder and duller than clanging - chains and machinery rather than bells.
examples: the clanking arms of the soldiers near him

entries.definition: made dirty or foul
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and disgusted, and it implies an agent: someone fouled this.

entries.definition: pleasing in appearance especially by reason of conformity to ideals of form and proportion
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises strong, well-proportioned looks; dignity rather than prettiness.
examples: very pretty but not so extraordinarily handsome

entries.definition: in a pretty manner
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *pretty*: pleasing but slight - delicate rather than striking, and faintly diminishing.
examples: all this is most prettily done

entries.definition: feeling happy appreciation
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The weakest claim here, and the one most easily said out of politeness.

entries.definition: in such a manner that death ensues (also in reference to hatred, jealousy, fear, etc.)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *mortal*: *A mortal enemy* - deadly rather than pitiless, and archaic in flavour.
examples: a being of whom the forest Indians are said to be mortally afraid, with a hoof shaped like the heel of a bottle

entries.definition: giving or spending with reluctance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same euphemism, now dated and chiefly British.
examples: very close (or near) with his money

entries.definition: poor enough to need help from others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Made poor - the word implies something was taken away.

entries.definition: very pleasing to the eye
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Old-fashioned approval of pleasant looks.

entries.definition: take illegally; of intellectual property
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Systematic, large-scale robbery - the word of armies and empires.
examples: This writer plundered from famous authors

entries.definition: being very thin
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Casual and unflattering - thin in a way that suggests too thin.
examples: a child with skinny freckled legs
He was a skinny kid who never filled out.

entries.definition: believing the worst of human nature and motives; having a sneering disbelief in e.g. selflessness of others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Assumes the worst motive as a general rule, which saves the trouble of looking.

entries.definition: (used colloquially) overly conceited or arrogant
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Playground-plain accusation of thinking yourself above others.
examples: they're snobs — stuck-up and uppity and persnickety

entries.definition: exhibiting courtesy and politeness
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Weak from overuse; it now praises so mildly that it can read as faint disappointment.

entries.definition: marked by skill in deception
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Has drifted to describing problems rather than people; of a person it is still a warning.

entries.definition: not of the highest quality or sophistication
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The clipped form, and rarer outside American speech.

entries.definition: characteristic of those having an inflated idea of their own importance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A clinical diagnosis used as an insult, which is what makes it land so hard.

entries.definition: characteristic of or befitting a friend
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The unarguable positive: it describes behaviour nobody objects to and implies nothing further.

entries.definition: characterized by kindness and warm courtesy especially of a king to his subjects
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Literary and top-down - warmth extended by someone with the power not to bother.

entries.definition: idle or indolent especially in a dreamy way
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Comic rather than damning; the failing is a lack of spirit, not of will.
examples: she was annoyingly lackadaisical and impractical

entries.definition: having undesirable or negative qualities
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain word of disapproval - broad and unemphatic.
examples: his sloppy appearance made a bad impression

entries.definition: in disarray; extremely disorderly
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Archaic and comic-sounding; using it is a decision.

entries.definition: (British informal) lacking intelligence and vitality
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British informal - vacant and hopeless with it.

entries.definition: with appreciation; in a grateful manner
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *grateful*: the plain word for the feeling, with no reservation in it.

entries.definition: lacking civility or good manners
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The everyday word, learned early, and blunt enough to be used to a child's face.

entries.definition: irritable as if suffering from indigestion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Black bile, straight from the four humours; unusable now without irony.

entries.definition: make off with belongings of others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Almost affectionate - taking something small and hardly worth the fuss.

entries.definition: lacking refinement or cultivation or taste
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pure class contempt - the word says more about the speaker than the subject.
examples: behavior that branded him as common

entries.definition: marked by refinement in taste and manners
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warmer and less effortful than cultivated; it suggests taste that was absorbed rather than studied.

entries.definition: in disarray; extremely disorderly
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Disorder that flatters - the one word here that can be arranged on purpose.
examples: his brown hair was tousled, thick, and curly

entries.definition: suffering from excessive eating or drinking
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Describes the sick aftermath rather than the appetite - more pitiable than blamed.

entries.definition: marked by skill in deception
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Cunning with the disapproval taken out - a wily negotiator is being complimented.

entries.definition: in utter disorder
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Older, rarer, and pulled between disorder and secrecy.

entries.definition: free from duties or responsibilities
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same idleness, admired - because it is assumed to have been paid for.
examples: even the artist and the sculptor were not regarded … as leisured men
